candidates.statement: The order service returns HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders, which the gateway surfaces as 502 on POST /v1/checkout; the fault originates in the order service, not the gateway.
candidates.uncertainty: Order-side logs/traces and the specific 500 cause (e.g. DB, payment, inventory) are not in evidence; only the gateway's view is observed.

report.explanation: Traces and logs consistently show gateway POST /v1/checkout returning 502 immediately after a downstream POST order call to http://order:8000/v1/orders returns 500, across multiple correlation IDs. Topology confirms gateway->order. The bounded candidate is an order-service HTTP 500 propagating to the gateway; the internal cause is not yet established.
missing_evidence: Order service logs/traces for POST /v1/orders to identify the internal 500 cause
Order service dependency metrics (postgresql, payment, inventory) to rule out db-pool-exhaustion or downstream-latency
